entries.reason: A seed counts only when the routine spares the scored people at least this much need above the threshold against waiting, per scored person, in need-thousandths times minutes; a comparison scores one group, of any size, so the floor is stated per person. It is the first protocol's floor of 4,600 for the small square's eight people, measured before any model was asked on the eight development seeds through the product's runner with a scripted model (the routine spared from 10,858 to 25,175, median 18,537.5; a quarter of the median, rounded down to the hundred), divided by the eight people it was measured over. A seed under it is excluded by name, never scored, so no seed on which the routine had almost nothing to spare decides a mean.

entries.reason: The most a seed's two runs may take to be read. Every read of a run replays it from what it stored and holds it to what it recorded, and the page reads a seed's two runs at once, saying meanwhile that it is replaying them, while one process replays the two one after the other, so each run's read is held to half of this. Ten seconds is the longest a person keeps their attention on a wait they are told about (Nielsen, Usability Engineering, 1993, chapter 5). The most people a comparison runs, and the most of them a model may decide for in one run, are derived from this and the four measured figures beside it (exulanica/world/society_comparison_reading.py), never stated.

entries.reason: What reading one run costs whatever its people, in the cost a run's read is estimated by: fixed + per person x population + per decided person x decided + per decided pair x population x decided. Measured with scripts/measure_comparison_replay.py inside quiet-slot then gpu-slot on tree 3d7bc30d with this protocol's change, the machine 92.7 percent idle before and 95.2 after and its one-minute load under 8 before every point: one simulated hour of a small town's society played once and read five times at each of 30 points, 8 to 128 people on the median (44 people) and the largest (56) of 20 towns' graphs, a model deciding for nobody, everybody, or 4, 8 or 16 of them. Of every such cost with no negative term that lies on or above every point's 95th percentile, this is the one whose margins over the points sum to the least, rounded up: it lies 1 ms above the closest point and at most 2.4 s above any.
